problem.summary: 单图像超分辨率（SISR）任务中，现有基于深度神经网络的方法通常先使用双三次插值等单一滤波器将低分辨率（LR）图像上采样到高分辨率（HR）空间，然后在HR空间进行重建。这种做法是次优的，并增加了计算复杂度。

motivation.summary: 在HR空间进行超分辨率操作计算成本高昂，且非自适应的上采样（如双三次插值）无法为重建问题提供额外信息。需要一种更高效、更有效的架构，能够在LR空间进行特征提取，并学习自适应的上采样滤波器。

core_idea.summary: 提出一种新颖的卷积神经网络架构（ESPCN），在LR空间进行特征提取，并在最后一层引入高效的亚像素卷积层（sub-pixel convolution layer），通过学习一组上采样滤波器，直接将LR特征图转换为HR输出图像。这避免了在HR空间进行大部分计算，显著降低了计算复杂度。

method.summary: 网络由多个卷积层在LR空间提取特征，最后一层是亚像素卷积层。该层对LR特征图进行卷积，生成通道数为C·r²的输出，然后通过周期性混洗（Periodic Shuffling, PS）操作将这些通道重新排列成rH×rW×C的HR图像。训练使用均方误差（MSE）作为损失函数。

experiments.summary: 在多个公开图像数据集（Set5, Set14, BSD300, BSD500, SuperTexture）和视频数据集（Xiph, Ultra Video Group）上进行了评估。与双三次插值、SRCNN和TNRD等方法进行了比较，评估了PSNR、运行时间和视觉质量。

claims.claim: 1. 在LR空间进行特征提取并使用亚像素卷积层进行上采样，比在HR空间进行操作更优且计算效率更高。2. ESPCN在图像和视频超分辨率任务上，比之前的CNN方法（如SRCNN）实现了显著的性能提升（图像+0.15dB，视频+0.39dB）和数量级的速度提升。3. 该方法能够在单个K2 GPU上实现1080p视频的实时超分辨率。

limitations.limitation: 论文未明确讨论方法的局限性。潜在的局限性可能包括：对特定上采样因子需要训练单独的网络；模型性能可能依赖于训练数据的质量和规模；以及对于非常大的上采样因子，性能可能下降。

nodes.title: 低分辨率输入
nodes.label: Input
nodes.summary: 网络的输入是低分辨率（LR）图像，尺寸为H×W×C。
nodes.description: 输入图像ILR，尺寸为H×W×C，其中C是颜色通道数。与之前方法不同，此输入直接进入网络，无需预先上采样。

nodes.title: LR空间特征提取
nodes.label: Feature Extraction
nodes.summary: 多个卷积层在低分辨率空间提取特征图。
nodes.description: 使用L-1个卷积层在LR空间进行特征提取。第l层的输出为f_l(I_LR; W_{1:l}, b_{1:l}) = φ(W_l * f_{l-1}(I_LR) + b_l)，其中φ是激活函数（如tanh），W_l和b_l是可学习参数。

nodes.title: 亚像素卷积层
nodes.label: Sub-pixel Convolution
nodes.summary: 最后一层卷积层，将LR特征图转换为HR图像。
nodes.description: 最后一层f_L对LR特征图进行卷积，生成一个H×W×(C·r²)的张量，其中r是上采样因子。该层不应用非线性激活函数。

nodes.title: 周期性混洗操作
nodes.label: Periodic Shuffling
nodes.summary: 将亚像素卷积层的输出重排为高分辨率图像。
nodes.description: 操作PS将形状为H×W×(C·r²)的张量T重排为形状为rH×rW×C的张量。数学描述为：PS(T)_{x,y,c} = T_{⌊x/r⌋, ⌊y/r⌋, C·r·mod(y,r) + C·mod(x,r) + c}。

nodes.title: 高分辨率输出
nodes.label: Output
nodes.summary: 网络的输出是重建的高分辨率（HR）图像，尺寸为rH×rW×C。
nodes.description: 最终输出的HR图像I_SR，尺寸为rH×rW×C。

nodes.title: 损失函数
nodes.label: Loss Function
nodes.summary: 使用像素级均方误差（MSE）作为训练目标。

edges.label: 输入特征
edges.description: 低分辨率图像输入到特征提取模块。

edges.label: 特征图
edges.description: LR空间提取的特征图传递到亚像素卷积层。

edges.label: 卷积输出
edges.description: 亚像素卷积层的输出（H×W×C·r²）传递到周期性混洗操作。

edges.label: 重排结果
edges.description: 周期性混洗操作生成最终的高分辨率图像。

edges.label: 预测输出
edges.description: 网络输出的HR图像用于计算与真实HR图像的损失。

deltas.before: 在HR空间进行特征提取和重建，计算复杂度高（与r²成正比）。
deltas.after: 在LR空间进行特征提取，仅在最后一层进行上采样，计算复杂度大幅降低。
deltas.why_it_matters: 显著减少了计算量和内存消耗，使得实时处理高分辨率视频成为可能。

deltas.before: 使用固定的、非自适应的上采样滤波器（如双三次插值）。
deltas.after: 使用可学习的、自适应的亚像素卷积滤波器，为每个特征图学习特定的上采样模式。
deltas.why_it_matters: 自适应滤波器能更好地重建高频细节，提升重建质量。

deltas.before: 上采样操作在网络开始前完成（预处理步骤）。
deltas.after: 上采样操作集成在网络的最后一层（亚像素卷积层）。
deltas.why_it_matters: 将上采样作为可学习的网络组件，实现了端到端的优化，并可能学习到更优的上采样策略。

formulas.intuition: 描述了网络中第l层（l < L）的前向传播过程。在低分辨率空间对输入或前一层特征图进行卷积，并应用非线性激活函数。

variables.name: f_L
variables.description: 最后一层（亚像素卷积层）的函数

variables.name: W_L
variables.description: 最后一层的卷积权重张量，形状为n_{L-1} × (C·r²) × k_L × k_L

formulas.intuition: 描述了最后一层的操作。首先对LR特征图进行卷积，生成通道数为C·r²的张量，然后通过周期性混洗操作将其重排为HR图像。这是实现高效上采样的关键。

formulas.latex: PS(T)_{x,y,c} = T_{\lfloor x/r \rfloor, \lfloor y/r \rfloor, C \cdot r \cdot \text{mod}(y,r) + C \cdot \text{mod}(x,r) + c}

variables.name: PS(T)
variables.description: 周期性混洗操作后的输出张量，形状为rH×rW×C

variables.name: c
variables.description: 输出图像的颜色通道索引

formulas.intuition: 定义了周期性混洗操作的具体数学形式。它将输入张量T中位于(⌊x/r⌋, ⌊y/r⌋)位置、特定通道组合的元素，映射到输出图像(x, y, c)位置。这实现了从LR特征图到HR图像的像素重排。

variables.name: f^L_{x,y}(I_{LR})
variables.description: 网络预测的HR图像在(x,y)位置的像素值

formulas.intuition: 训练网络使用的损失函数。计算预测的HR图像与真实HR图像之间所有像素的均方误差。这是驱动网络学习重建能力的优化目标。

terms.definition: 单图像超分辨率（Single Image Super-Resolution），从单张低分辨率图像重建高分辨率图像的任务。
高效亚像素卷积神经网络（Efficient Sub-Pixel Convolutional Neural Network），本文提出的网络架构。
本文提出的一种新型网络层，通过卷积和周期性混洗操作，直接将LR特征图转换为HR图像。
一种操作，将形状为H×W×(C·r²)的张量重排为形状为rH×rW×C的张量，实现从LR特征图到HR图像的像素重排。
图像分辨率放大的倍数。
峰值信噪比（Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio），衡量图像重建质量的指标，单位为dB，值越高越好。

steps.description: 1. 数据准备：下载并预处理训练（91张图像或ImageNet）和测试数据集。生成LR-HR图像对（通过高斯模糊和下采样）。
2. 模型实现：根据论文描述实现ESPCN网络架构，包括LR空间卷积层和亚像素卷积层（含周期性混洗操作）。
3. 训练：使用MSE损失函数训练网络。设置学习率（初始0.01，最终0.0001），最后一层学习率降低10倍。训练直至收敛（约100个epoch无改善后停止）。
4. 评估：在测试数据集上计算PSNR。比较运行时间（在K2 GPU上）。
5. 视频处理：将训练好的模型应用于视频帧，实现逐帧超分辨率。

metadata.title: Real-Time Single Image and Video Super-Resolution Using an Efficient Sub-Pixel Convolutional Neural Network
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / Pose Estimation / Computer Vision / Video Understanding / Computer Vision / CNN / Computer Vision / Top-cited Computer Vision paper
metadata.abstract: Recently, several models based on deep neural networks have achieved great success in terms of both reconstruction accuracy and computational performance for single image super-resolution. In these methods, the low resolution (LR) input image is upscaled to the high resolution (HR) space using a single filter, commonly bicubic interpolation, before reconstruction. This means that the super-resolution (SR) operation is performed in HR space. We demonstrate that this is sub-optimal and adds computational complexity. In this paper, we present the first convolutional neural network (CNN) capable of real-time SR of 1080p videos on a single K2 GPU. To achieve this, we propose a novel CNN architecture where the feature maps are extracted in the LR space. In addition, we introduce an efficient sub-pixel convolution layer which learns an array of upscaling filters to upscale the final LR feature maps into the HR output. By doing so, we effectively replace the handcrafted bicubic filter in the SR pipeline with more complex upscaling filters specifically trained for each feature map, whilst also reducing the computational complexity of the overall SR operation. We evaluate the proposed approach using images and videos from publicly available datasets and show that it performs significantly better (+0.15dB on Images and +0.39dB on Videos) and is an order of magnitude faster than previous CNN-based methods.

Recently, several models based on deep neural networks have achieved great success in terms of both reconstruction accuracy and computational performance for single image super-resolution. In these methods, the low resolution (LR) input image is upscaled to the high resolution (HR) space using a single ﬁlter, commonly bicubic interpolation, before reconstruction. In this paper, we present the ﬁrst convolutional neural network (CNN) capable of real-time SR of 1080p videos on a single K2 GPU. To achieve this, we propose a novel CNN architec- ture where the feature maps are extracted in the LR space. In addition, we introduce an efﬁcient sub-pixel convolution layer which learns an array of upscaling ﬁlters to upscale the ﬁnal LR feature maps into the HR output. A key assumption that underlies many SR techniques is that much of the high-frequency data is redundant and thus can be accurately reconstructed from low frequency components. SR is therefore an inference problem, and thus relies on our model of the statistics of images in question. Many methods assume multiple images are available as LR instances of the same scene with different perspectives, i.e. with unique prior afﬁne transformations. These can be categorised as multi-image SR methods [1, 11] and exploit explicit redundancy by constraining the ill-posed problem with additional information and attempting to invert the downsampling process. However, these methods usually require computationally complex image registration and fusion stages, the accuracy of which directly impacts the quality of the result. A detailed review of more generic SISR methods can be found in [45]. One family of approaches that has recently thrived in tackling the SISR problem is sparsity-based techniques. Sparse coding is an effective mechanism that assumes any natural image can be sparsely represented in a transform domain. This transform domain is usually a dictionary of image atoms [25, 10], which can be learnt through a training process that tries to discover the correspondence between LR and HR patches. This dictionary is able to embed the prior knowledge necessary to constrain the ill-posed problem of super-resolving unseen data. This approach is proposed in the methods of [47, 8]. Motivations and contributions With the development of CNN, the efﬁciency of the al- gorithms, especially their computational and memory cost, gains importance [36]. The ﬂexibility of deep network mod- els to learn nonlinear relationships has been shown to attain superior reconstruction accuracy compared to previously hand-crafted models [27, 7, 44, 31, 3]. To super-resolve a LR image into HR space, it is necessary to increase the resolution of the LR image to match that of the HR image at some point. In Osendorfer et al. In general, both ILR and IHR can have C colour channels, thus they are represented as real-valued tensors of sizeH×W×C andrH×rW×C, respectively. To solve the SISR problem, the SRCNN proposed in [7] recovers from an upscaled and interpolated version of ILR instead of ILR. To recover ISR, a 3 layer convolutional network is used. In this section we propose a novel network architecture, as illustrated in Fig. 1, to avoid upscaling ILR before feeding it into the network. In our architecture, we ﬁrst apply al layer convolutional neural network directly to the LR image, and then apply a sub-pixel convolution layer that upscales the LR feature maps to produce ISR. This approach has been successfully used in visualizing layer activations [49] and for generating semantic segmentations using high level features from the network [24]. It is trivial to show that the bicubic interpolation used in SRCNN is a special case of the deconvolution layer, as suggested already in [24, 7]. The deconvolution layer proposed in [50] can be seen as multiplication of each input pixel by a ﬁlter element-wise with stride r, and sums over the resulting output windows also known as backwards convolution [24].

For the ESPCN, we set l = 3 , (f1,n 1) = (5 , 64),
(f2,n 2) = (3 , 32) and f3 = 3 in our evaluations. The

choice of the parameter is inspired by SRCNN’s 3 layer 9-5- 5 model and the equations in Sec. 2.2. In the training phase, 17r× 17r pixel sub-images are extracted from the training ground truth images IHR, where r is the upscaling factor. To synthesize the low-resolution samplesILR, we blur IHR using a Gaussian ﬁlter and sub-sample it by the upscaling factor. The sub-images are extracted from original images
with a stride of (17−∑mod (f, 2))×r from IHR and a
stride of 17−∑mod (f, 2) from ILR. This ensures that

all pixels in the original image appear once and only once as the ground truth of the training data. We choose tanh instead ofrelu as the activation function for the ﬁnal model motivated by our experimental results. The training stops after no improvement of the cost function is observed after 100 epochs. Initial learning rate is set to 0.01 and ﬁnal learning rate is set to 0.0001 and updated gradually when the improvement of the cost function is smaller than a threshold µ. The ﬁnal layer learns 10 times slower as in [7]. The training takes roughly three hours on a K2 GPU on 91 images, and seven days on images from ImageNet [30] for upscaling factor of 3. We use the PSNR as the performance metric to evaluate our models. PSNR of SRCNN and Chen’s models on our extended benchmark set are calculated based on the Matlab code and models provided by [7, 3]. 3.3. Run time evaluations In this section, we evaluated our best model’s run time on Set144 with an upscale factor of 3. We evaluate the run time of other methods [2, 51, 39] from the Matlab codes provided by [40] and [31]. For methods which use convolutions in- cluding our own, a python/theano implementation is used to improve the efﬁciency based on the Matlab codes provided in [7, 3]. The results are presented in Fig. 2. Our model runs a magnitude faster than the fastest methods published so far. Compared to SRCNN 9-5-5 ImageNet model, the number of convolution required to super-resolve one image isr×r times smaller and the number of total parameters of the model is 2.5 times smaller. We have achieved a stunning average speed of 4.7ms for super-resolving one single image fromSet14 on a K2 GPU. Utilising the amazing speed of the network, it will be inter- esting to explore ensemble prediction using independently trained models as discussed in [36] to achieve better SR performance in the future. We also evaluated run time of 1080 HD video super- resolution using videos from the Xiph and the Ultra Video Group database. Conclusion In this paper, we demonstrate that a non-adaptive up- scaling at the ﬁrst layer provides worse results than an adaptive upscaling for SISR and requires more computa- tional complexity. To address the problem, we propose to perform the feature extraction stages in the LR space instead of HR space.
